html:
Three-day stand by a small Greek force against the huge army of Xerxes at the narrow pass of Thermopylae, in central Greece, in 480 BCE.

The Greek commander was the Spartan king Leonidas, with about 7,000 men from many cities, among them 300 Spartan citizen soldiers. In the pass the Persians could not use their numbers. They lost many men in frontal attacks. A local man, Ephialtes, then showed them a mountain path behind the Greek line.

Leonidas sent most of the army away and stayed with the 300 Spartans, about 700 men from Thespiae, and some Thebans. They fought to the death. The Greek fleet fought the Persian navy at Artemisium over the same days, then fell back.

Thermopylae was a military defeat. It bought time, and it gave the Greeks a story of courage. The Persians burned Athens soon after, but the Greeks won at sea at Salamis, led by themistocles, and on land at Plataea in 479 BCE. The pass was named the gate of Greece for good reason: it was the main road south.
sum: Three-day stand by a small Greek force against the huge army of Xerxes at the narrow pass of Thermopylae, in central Greece, in 480 BCE.
